summary: Client-only results of the 'mon' debug monitor's mon::SubgridEdgeRequestComponent (AI subgrid edge display). Registered by bg3.exe+0x11EE9F0 (size 0x10, align 0x10) with destructor thunk_FUN_1405946c0 = the plain-Array destructor (frees the buffer, no per-element work). No system of bg3.exe or of the Toolkit DLLs fills or reads it, so the element type and stride cannot be established; the array is written as its three raw members. Never seen alive.

fields.name: Data
fields.evidence: bg3.exe+0x5946C0 (destructor registered by bg3.exe+0x11EE9F0): frees the pointer at +0 when capacity +8 != 0 = buffer of an Array of trivially destructible elements; element type unknown.

fields.name: Capacity
fields.evidence: bg3.exe+0x5946C0 tests +8 before freeing and resets it to 0.

open_questions: Element type and stride of the array (probably edge segments: pairs of positions) - no producer in the shipped binaries; macOS destructor (bg3_macos_x64+0x25D9750) is also element-free.
status_reason: no live or captured instance: needs a situation that creates it
second_pass: Cannot be settled from code: the second pass found no producer or consumer anywhere - bg3.exe has only the type registration (App::CreateECS -> bg3.exe+0x11EExxx), the static type-name initialiser and the component ops; the macOS build has only ComponentOps/ComponentSignals/destructor instantiations (macos_index.py names '<mon::' lists just the eight mon types) and the Toolkit DLLs mention them only in App::AddGlobalSwitchesToOptionDialog. The shapes from the creator/destructor stand; the members stay unknown.
